clue.text: Party maiden at home — troublesome female, bully

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
in means at home, as in 'staying in'
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A list of party guests: a young woman who stayed home, and a difficult woman who pushed everyone around.
explanation.walkthrough: ATE, the Greek goddess who led people into reckless folly, is a crossword favourite for a troublesome female.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully someone is to lord it over them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Senior woman has info on artist providing entertainment

parts.note: a gran is a grandmother, an older woman
dope is slang for inside information
RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: An elderly woman has the lowdown on a painter, and it makes for good entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera on the grand scale, sung throughout, is one kind of staged entertainment.

clue.text: Act to keep carpet unfortunately pulled to pieces

indicators.note: a word that keeps something holds it within itself, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: a deed is an act or action

indicators.note: something gone wrong unfortunately is in disorder, so the letters of carpet are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone acts to save a carpet that has sadly been torn apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges the letters of the word carpet, and 'to keep' holds that inside the act. 'pulled to pieces' sounds like the torn carpet but means criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deprecated has been disparaged or run down, the figurative sense of criticised harshly.

clue.text: What twister effects with empty words

definitions.meaning: a tornado or twister is a violent whirling air current, so it produces a gale of moving air
talk that is all bluster and no substance, hot air

explanation.surface: A tornado's damage, described in meaningless words.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving air is what a twister makes, and idle bluster is called this in idiom too.

clue.text: Ruth maybe in a confusing situation endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a babel is a scene of noisy confusion, after the Tower of Babel

explanation.surface: A woman called Ruth gets caught up in a never-ending muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' looks like a woman's name, but it points to Babe Ruth, the American baseball star.
explanation.definitionFit: Babe was the nickname of the baseball player Ruth, so Ruth is an example of a Babe.

clue.text: Teases youngsters

definitions.meaning: to kid someone is to tease or josh them, verb sense
children, informally called this, plural noun sense

explanation.definitionFit: Kidding is joking teasing, and kids are children; one spelling serves as verb and noun.

clue.text: Report of army officer being a bit of a nut

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so this signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: a colonel is a senior army officer, pronounced like the inner part of a seed

explanation.surface: A tale of a military man who is somewhat eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of a nut' looks like 'somewhat crazy', but it is the edible inner part of a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft edible centre inside a nutshell is its core part, the seed.

clue.text: It's bitter, attending church in spring

indicators.note: attending means going along beside, so one piece is placed next to the other

parts.note: sour means bitter in taste
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone sour-tempered goes to church in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season, but it is a spring of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring is where a stream rises, its origin or fountainhead.

clue.text: Bradman's opposing crossword checker? Not really true!

parts.note: the setter's name with 's stands for 'I am', shortened to I'm
agin is a dialect word meaning against
the editor, ED, checks a crossword before it is published

explanation.surface: The setter claims to oppose the puzzle editor, which is surely a fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: Bradman is this puzzle's setter, so 'Bradman's' means 'I'm'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreamt up exists only in the mind, so it is not actually real.

clue.text: Demeanour of soldiers crossing India

indicators.note: the soldiers cross, or span, the letter, so it sits inside them

parts.note: men means soldiers, ordinary ranks
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The bearing of troops as they cross India.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's bearing or outward manner is a literary synonym for demeanour.

clue.text: Making good action to improve attire?

definitions.meaning: putting right a wrong or setting a grievance straight
putting clothes on again, a fresh outfit

explanation.definitionFit: Redress is compensation or putting right, and changing clothes again is literally dressing anew.

clue.text: Old pet maybe returning for food

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a cat is an example of a pet

explanation.surface: An elderly pet comes home for its dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican folded tortilla with a filling is a kind of food.

clue.text: Chopped pear covered in cold cheese

indicators.note: one piece is covered by another, so it sits inside it

parts.note: chilly means cold

indicators.note: chopped means cut up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cooking note: diced pear served with chilled cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopped' rearranges the fruit's letters, and 'covered in' places them inside the word for cold; the cheese takes its name from a Welsh town.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumbly white Welsh variety named after a town near Cardiff, an example of cheese.

clue.text: Planet's core — hot, going right down

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter moves all the way to the bottom, the end of the word

parts.note: the heart of something is its core
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: The planet's interior is hot, the heat sinking right down into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going right down' moves the H from the start of HEART to the bottom of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Our home world is the third planet from the Sun.

clue.text: Comic traveller and daughter see madam?

definitions.note: the question mark shows this word is an example: it reads the same backwards

parts.note: Michael Palin, a Monty Python comedian later famous for travel documentaries
the Holy See has its seat in this Italian city, a bishop's see being his diocese

explanation.surface: A comedian on his travels takes his daughter to meet a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like a verb, but it is a see, the Pope's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word madam reads identically in either direction, an example of such a word.

clue.text: Pity Mollie being treated in a rude manner

indicators.note: something being treated is being processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone feels sorry for Mollie, who was handled discourteously.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting discourteously means behaving rudely, the adverb matching the phrase.

clue.text: Some territory's internal boundary

indicators.note: internal means inside, so the answer lies within the words

explanation.surface: A description of a dividing line drawn within part of a territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like the hidden-word signal, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A mete is an old word for a limit or boundary mark, kept alive in the legal phrase metes and bounds.

clue.text: Wandering up this mountainous region — poultry?

indicators.note: wandering means straying about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram, read backwards from the answer: UP plus this region gives this word

explanation.surface: Chickens roaming up a mountain district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wandering' shuffles UP together with the answer to give POULTRY, so take UP out of POULTRY and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An Alpine area of western Austria and northern Italy is a mountainous region.

clue.text: See 26
Showered in small room atop one outhouse

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting atop another comes first

parts.note: lav is short for lavatory, a small room
I is the Roman numeral one
a shed is an outbuilding

explanation.surface: Someone had a shower in a tiny room perched on an outbuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showered' looks like washing, but here it means heaped upon.
explanation.definitionFit: To lavish gifts is to shower them generously on someone.

clue.text: Hand went on twitching periodically

indicators.note: twitching means moving jerkily, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hand kept twitching, on and off.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for occasionally, at intervals rather than all the time.

clue.text: Confessing Cambridge college should sack its head

indicators.note: sacking the head means dismissing the first letter of the word

parts.note: Downing is a college of Cambridge University

explanation.surface: A Cambridge college admits it should dismiss its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Owning up to something means admitting or confessing it.

clue.text: Survive with organ not right

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: the liver is a bodily organ

explanation.surface: Someone is getting by despite a failing organ.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay alive or carry on existing is a plain synonym for survive.

clue.text: Awful crude fan men ignored

indicators.note: awful means in a bad state, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means men as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: A crass supporter and his mates are being snubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' turns CRUDE FAN into UNCAREDF, then OR is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Something neglected and left without attention has been ignored.

clue.text: Tree, one hanging over river

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece hanging over the other sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A tree with a branch that overhangs a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The maples belong to this botanical genus, so it names a kind of tree.

clue.text: People facing way-out questions during an election

definitions.text: People facing way-out questions during an election

parts.words: People facing way-out questions during an election
parts.note: voters leaving the ... station are asked how they voted

explanation.definitionFit: A survey taken of voters as they leave the booth asks questions at the way out.

clue.text: Sack with wood on bottom of grate

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: fir is a kind of wood

indicators.note: the bottom of a word in a down clue is its last letter

explanation.surface: A sack of firewood placed on the base of a grate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like a bag of logs, but it means dismiss.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack someone is to dismiss them from a job.

clue.text: Match put back with first hint of trouble

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: set means put or placed

indicators.note: the first hint of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A sports fixture postponed at the first sign of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' looks like postponed; 'back' turns SET around.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket test is an international match.

clue.text: Deduce backward-looking French king is not so good

parts.note: to infer is to deduce

indicators.note: looking backward means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: roi is French for king

explanation.surface: A conclusion that a nostalgic French monarch is not up to scratch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of lower quality is worse, so less good than another.

clue.text: Something hairy and out of this world east of island

indicators.note: in an across clue east of means to the right, so it comes after

parts.note: Mull is an island of the Inner Hebrides off Scotland
ET is the extraterrestrial of the film

explanation.surface: Something hairy and alien lands east of an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A haircut short at the front and long at the back is a hairy example.
